Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-02 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Rivera (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (Redwood CSM), Anika Bose (Polar Head of Partnerships), Tom Reilly (VP Sales), Sanaa Karim (Solutions Architect), Diego Marquez (Legal), Priya Nair (RevOps)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got a packed agenda. quick intros?
[00:07] Anika Bose: hi all, Anika here, Polar partnerships. good to see you. sorry about background noise, had a kid drop a toy.
[00:12] Tom Reilly: Tom, VP sales, will be running the co-sell motion w/ maya and anika from our side.
[00:16] Lucas Rivera: Lucas, solutions engineering at Redwood. i'll focus on perf and architecture questions today.
[00:20] Sanaa Karim: Sanaa, solutions architect at Polar, i'll be technical contact.
[00:24] Diego Marquez: Diego, legal -- short on time but i'll flag blocker items.
[00:30] Maya Chen: great, goal for today: triage two priority opps, align on playbook and outstanding gating items. start with opportunity A - large enterprise ID manage product.
[02:04] Tom Reilly: rough numbers: 500 seat pilot, move to 5k seats in 9 months, expected 2-3M ARR over 18 months. big ask is SSO/SCIM and on-prem-ish data locality for logs.
[02:25] Lucas Rivera: ok, primary question: do you expect inference to be in your VPC or is hostable?
[02:33] Sanaa Karim: they'd prefer VPC or dedicated infra for PII. but initial pilot could be hosted if logs never leave redwood's systems, which is tricky.
[03:01] Maya Chen: quick note - Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem variants; but the rollout cost/time differs. we usually propose hosted for speed, then dedicated as commit grows.
[03:28] Anika Bose: what's the timeline tradeoff typically? legal wants a clear checkbox list.
[03:35] Asha Patel: from other partners it's about 4-8 weeks for hosted integration, 8-14 weeks for dedicated/VPC depending on certs and KMS integration.
[04:12] Diego Marquez: we need to see SOC2 Type II report, KMS integration detail, and an audit log retention policy. if those are ok probably no sig blockers.
[04:29] Maya Chen: we can send SOC2 and our security pack; for KMS we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS providers, and HSM in private deployments.
[05:00] Sanaa Karim: any known latency numbers for region eu-west-1 vs us-central for token-forwarding?
[05:12] Lucas Rivera: median tail latencies depend on model. for a typical redwood-curated 7b we see p50 ~75ms p95 ~260ms in eu-west on dedicated nodes. hosted can be similar but depends on multi-tenant load and burst profile.
[05:32] Anika Bose: competitor question: will Anthropic or OpenAI integrations be part of the joint pitch?
[05:40] Maya Chen: we mention model-flexibility as a value prop - customers can choose variants or fallbacks, but jointly we'll pitch Redwood runtime + partner UX.
[06:05] Tom Reilly: keep an eye on cost objections, they always ask when we say dedicated.
[06:12] Lucas Rivera: cost buckets: model compute, token egress, and infra reservation. we can show delta between hosted and dedicated. i'll run 3-case modelling.
[07:10] Anika Bose: opp B is smaller: startup with real-time chat for customer service, 50 seats, but high concurrency and strict 99.9 latency SLOs.
[07:25] Lucas Rivera: that one probably needs dedicated pooled GPUs or dedicated shards with autoscale and smart batching disabled for latency. possible but costly.
[07:40] Sanaa Karim: can we do hybrid routing? e.g., low-latency tier hits dedicated, fallback to hosted for unusual spikes?
[07:48] Maya Chen: yes that's a standard pattern we recommend: primary route to dedicated with fallback to hosted. we can also do model variant fallback to a smaller quantized model to reduce costs in spikes.
[08:15] Tom Reilly: legal concern: data residency, logs, and debug artifacts. can we redact/limit logging for partner demos?
[08:23] Diego Marquez: exact ask: demo data must be anonymized and not leave customer infra; if Redwood needs logs for debugging we need an NDA and limited retention.
[08:38] Maya Chen: understood. propose: we provision demo environment with synthetic/anonymized records, and we can sign a demo-only NDA. i'll own that.
[09:00] Anika Bose: good. also want to understand the partner compensation motion -- is there co-sell credit, joint-sales credit?
[09:10] Maya Chen: Redwood offers a partner motion that includes joint credit for referrals + co-sell commission tiers; we'll share standard program doc.
[09:26] Priya Nair: from revops: we need clear lead routing rules and attribution sys. does redwood support CRM webhooks or partner portal?
[09:35] Asha Patel: we have partner portal integrations and can push to salesforce via webhooks; also SSO for partner accounts.
[10:20] Lucas Rivera: technical deep dive: for the enterprise ID manage product, sequence length is moderate but KV cache hit matters because many prompts reuse context. we recommend prefix caching and a mid-token quantized model for cost-savings.
[10:45] Sanaa Karim: what's the expected savings with quantization?
[10:50] Lucas Rivera: rough ballpark, 2x cost reduction on infer per-token for 4-bit quantization at small quality tradeoff; we'll add exact numbers in estimate.
[11:12] Tom Reilly: objection we see: partner wants a clean pilot handoff — we need a checklist: onboarding steps, success metrics, and rollback plan.
[11:22] Maya Chen: propose playbook items: kickoff, data-mining for prompt sets, bench test (1000 samples), pilot run, metric review (latency/cost/accuracy), then production migration. i'll send a templated checklist.
[12:05] Anika Bose: can Redwood support partner co-branded docs and a joint case study if pilot succeeds?
[12:12] Maya Chen: yes, we typically do customer stories with joint approvals.
[12:45] Diego Marquez: quick legal flag: indemnity and data processor terms — our legal will want to see Redwood's DPA and some carveouts.
[12:54] Maya Chen: we have standard DPA; i'll attach it. for carveouts we'll highlight what's negotiable.
[13:30] Lucas Rivera: on ops — autoscaling policies matter. if you want low p95 we may limit batch sizes and scale capacity; that increases cost. need to choose SLOs.
[13:50] Sanaa Karim: their SLO is 99.9 p95 < 300ms for chat, can that be met?
[13:58] Lucas Rivera: feasible on dedicated with right instance sizing, regional colocations; i'll model the instance mix.
[15:02] Maya Chen: rounding out, we should decide gating list for go/no-go for both opps. propose minimum: security pack reviewed, perf estimates for expected loads, NDA for demo, and clarified commercial split.
[15:20] Anika Bose: agreed. also want a short joint one-pager we can show customer with responsibilities.
[15:30] Maya Chen: we will draft a joint one-pager.
[16:45] Tom Reilly: timeline check: can we get perf estimates and playbook by next Friday? (2026-12-10)
[16:52] Lucas Rivera: yes i'll prioritize that.
[17:10] Diego Marquez: legal will need DPA and demo NDA by Monday, otherwise we can't show live data.
[17:20] Maya Chen: i'll push DPA and a demo NDA template today.
[18:00] Asha Patel: also planning a joint enablement call for partner reps — suggest week of 12/13, demo day.
[18:08] Anika Bose: works for us.
[18:20] Maya Chen: any other blockers?
[18:24] Sanaa Karim: one tiny thing — model explainability: the customer cares about auditing outputs. do you have a trace for tokens + decisioning?
[18:34] Lucas Rivera: we capture request traces, prompt/response payloads (optional) and can surface token-level attribution in our observability console; for private deployments traces can be kept in customer infra per KMS policies.
[19:01] Tom Reilly: perfect.
[19:25] Maya Chen: ok final recap: maya will send playbook, DPA, and NDA template; lucas will produce perf/cost estimates by 2026-12-10; asha will draft enablement timeline; anika to schedule demo week; diego to confirm NDA scope.
[19:40] Anika Bose: confirmed. thanks everyone.
[19:45] Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the demo and send artifacts. end call.
